unit: mantissa bits short of IEEE fp32, = log2 of the ratio between our reading and a better-precision counterpart of the SAME quantity. The cancellation factor cancels out of such a ratio, which is why the two sites are comparable at all.
unit_validated_by: LADDER_SHAPE.json -- a 2-bit-short accumulator reads 3.928 against a predicted 4.000, flat in K over a 2,300x span
verdict: NOT one mechanism at one magnitude. The softmax sites sit 12.3 to 17.6 bits short of IEEE fp32; the trunk reduction sits 1.6 to 2.2. The nearest pair is 10.1 bits apart, a factor of 1121. Both are on-device precision deficits and both are consistent with TT fp32 being short of IEEE fp32, but they are not the same ceiling and the trunk will not be fixed by whatever fixes the softmax.
consequence: The trunk's deficit is SMALL -- about two bits. That is the opposite of the softmax finding, where nothing on-device came within four orders of magnitude of real fp32 and a host round trip was the only route. A two-bit deficit is the size a higher-precision on-device accumulate could plausibly close, so of3t-lnreduce should price the on-device rung BEFORE assuming it needs a host reduction. Testable, and cheaper if it holds.
caveat: The two readings are different computations -- a softmax output against float64, and a reduction's dW against upstream's own bf16 step -- so this is an order-of-magnitude argument in a common unit, not a proof. It is decisive only because the gap is 10.1 bits, far beyond what the shape difference plausibly explains.
